feedback.problem: A point $P$ has Cartesian coordinates $(-\frac{k}{4},\frac{k}{2}),$ where $k$ is a positive real number. What are the polar coordinates of $P?$ Round your answer to the nearest integer where necessary.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we determine $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{k}{4})}^{2}+{(\frac{k}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{k}^{2}}{16}+\frac{{k}^{2}}{4}} \\  & =\sqrt{5\cdot \frac{{k}^{2}}{16}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}\,k}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

For the reference angle, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{R} & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{(\frac{k}{2})}{(-\frac{k}{4})})| \\  & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-2)| \\  & ≈1.107.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the point $P$ lies in the second quadrant, we subtract the reference angle from $\pi $ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta  & =\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi -1.107 \\  & ≈2.035 \\  & ≈2,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer. Therefore, the polar coordinates of $P$ are $(\frac{\sqrt{5}\,k}{4},2).$
